facts.text: Waterloo was initially settled in 1848 by Elmore Kees, who built a flouring mill, a sawmill, and a trading post.
The city's name is a joking reference to the Battle of Waterloo following a nineteenth-century court decision over a land dispute.
The federal government established a post office at Waterloo on January 5, 1875, with Granger serving as the first postmaster.
Waterloo developed amid Linn County's agricultural expansion, originally tied to milling operations along the South Santiam River.
Waterloo's landscape features grasslands, forage crops, and scattered oak woodlands adapted to Mediterranean-influenced conditions.
The region around Waterloo experiences warm and dry summers, with average monthly temperatures staying below 71.6 degrees Fahrenheit.
